3. In order to bring home the guilt of appellant, the prosecution has examined as many as 23 witnesses victim (PW-1), Kanshram Nisad (PW-2),Santoshi Nisad (PW-3), Mamta Dhivar (PW-4),
Narsingh Nisad (PW-5), Anant Nisad (PW-6), Nandlal Nisad (PW-7), Santosh Nisad (PW-8), Dr.
Karuna Awade (PW-9), Kunti Bai (PW-10), Reshamlal (PW-11), Roman Chandravanshi (PW-12),
Praveen Dhivar (PW-13), Dhanusram (PW-14), Mahesh Sahu (PW-15), Santosh (PW-16),

S.S.
Thakur (PW-17), Lekhram Chandrakar (PW- 18), Nammu Dhivar (PW-19), Purushottam Sahu (PW-20), Padmavati Sahu (PW-21), Chitralekha Navrange (PW-22), Santoshi Agrawal (PW-23).

4. Victim (PW-1) was examined before the Court wherein she has stated that the appellant took her to Khallari temple where he performed forceful marriage with her thereafter he made forceful sexual intercourse with her on many times.
Thereafter he took her to new Raipur where they stayed at newly constructed building at Sector No. 24 where he also committed sexual intercourse with her.
Thereafter, Police recovered her from the possession of the appellant.
5. PW-4 and other witnesses have reiterated the stand taken by the victim in her evidence and they have fully supported the case of the prosecution.
The trial Court on the basis of material, evidence on record has stated that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt and convicted the appellant as mentioned above.

6. Counsel for the appellant would submit that the prosecution has not proved its case beyond reasonable doubt and and without there being any iota of evidence, the trial Court has convicted the appellant.

He would further submit that there is omission and contradiction in the prosecution witness which is overlooked by the trial Court and would pray for set aside the judgment of conviction and order of sentence.

7. Per contra learned counsel for the state would submit that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt, therefore, the order impugned does not suffer from any irregularly or infirmity warranting interference by this Court in the instant appeal.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

9. Considering the fact I am of the considered opinion that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt so far as it relates to offence punishable under Section 363 and 366-A of Ajay Kumar Sonwani vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179504560/

So far as it relations to offence punishable under Sections 366 of IPC and Section 6 of the POCSO Act that the appellant has kidnapped the victim and committed penetrative sexual assault on the pretext of marriage with the victim, as such No illegality or irregularity is found in the judgment.
Hence, is liable to be rejected and it is rejected.

10. It is reported that the appellant has been released from jail on 20.11.2024 after getting the benefit of remission and completing sentence awarded to him by the trial court as such the instant appeal so far as appellant is dismissed.
